title: Onprem / Air-gapped runtime deep dive - AtlasBank
summary: Deep technical session covering artifact delivery options for air-gapped AtlasBank environment, offline licensing flow, GPU driver compatibility and packaging, plus runtime performance tuning: KV/prefix cache behavior, batching strategies and quantization tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: provide artifact checklist, driver compatibility matrix, pilot scope and schedule benchmark run in AtlasBank lab.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~90 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Mark Davis (CTO, AtlasBank), Leah Wong (Infra), Ravi Menon (Security)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'll do a quick intro then pass to Priya for the deep dive. we know AtlasBank is fully air-gapped in a lot of sites so today's specifically about artifact delivery, offline licensing, and the GPU driver story plus runtime perf tips.

[00:20] Mark Davis: Yep thanks Alex. we've been working on the procurement approvals, wanted to make sure the SE level details line up with our security folks. Ravi is on to ask the tough questions.

[00:35] Priya Kapoor: Great, quick agenda: 1) artifact packaging and transfer options (OCI images vs tarball, signed checksums, HDD drop-off) 2) offline license flow and entitlement files 3) GPU driver compat + prebuilt kernels and 4) runtime perf: kv cache, batching, quantization tradeoffs and recommended pilot tests.

[01:00] Ravi Menon: Quick clarifier, we cannot have outbound internet from the cluster. all signatures and integrity checks must be verifiable locally, and we may require HSM-wrapped license keys.

[01:15] Priya Kapoor: Totally understood. Our air-gapped bundle supports both: signed tarball with detached signature and a license file that can be wrapped with customer public key. we also support a labeled encrypted license blob which you can unwrap with your HSM. we'll include a verification tool in the bundle that computes checksums and validates signatures locally.

[02:05] Leah Wong: For the artifact delivery, is Redwood providing container images or do we need to host them internally? what's recommended for upgrades?

[02:20] Alex Chen: Two options. 1) We give you tarballs of OCI images plus a local registry manifest; you import into your internal registry. 2) We provide raw tarball + system packages for offline install. For upgrades we provide delta patch bundles to minimize copy sizes if you want regular updates.

[03:05] Priya Kapoor: On drivers: we test and validate against a matrix of NVIDIA drivers (for the GPU SKUs we support). we'll send a driver compatibility matrix that lists certified driver versions, recommended CUDA/CuDNN, and the prebuilt kernel modules that we ship for common kernels. if you run a custom kernel we provide build instructions and a precompiled option.

[03:45] Mark Davis: Our infra team uses RHEL 8.6 with a slightly locked kernel (we backport). can you support building modules against a pinned kernel?

[04:00] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we can produce a driver bundle built against your specific kernel ABI if you provide the exact version. it's a small extra step in the air-gap pipeline; we'll do an iterative test in the pilot.

[04:30] Ravi Menon: About licensing - how does offline activation and renewal work? We need audit trails and a way to rotate keys without internet exposure.

[04:45] Alex Chen: Offline license flow we use: Redwood issues an entitlement file tied to a host fingerprint or attestation blob. You import the entitlement file and the runtime validates locally. For rotation we can generate a new entitlement signed by Redwood; the customer can sign the request blob with their key for attestation if you need that extra step. All events are logged locally and we provide a signed activation record that you can keep in your audit logs.

[05:30] Priya Kapoor: We'll include an offline renewal runbook: create CSR-like attestation file -> Redwood returns new entitlement -> import. We also support time-limited licenses for pilots.

[06:00] Leah Wong: For the artifact size: how big is the runtime tarball for a typical medium model runtime with prebuilt kernels? our transfer window is limited to a single encrypted HDD, prefer <200GB if possible.

[06:15] Priya Kapoor: Typical full bundle with model weights will be bigger; but for the runtime + engine + drivers without model artifacts, we usually see 6-18GB. Model weights depend on model family: a 30B model weights tarball could be 60-90GB. for pilot we recommend using a smaller quantized variant to keep transfer manageable.

[07:00] Mark Davis: Can you explain the quantization tradeoffs? we need to maintain a specific latency SLO for customer-facing features.

[07:15] Priya Kapoor: Sure - quantization (we support several profiles) can reduce memory and increase throughput. 4-bit/8-bit quantization gives a big win in throughput but can introduce small quality regressions. For inference runtime we recommend starting with 8-bit QAT or PTQ profiles validated on your eval set. We'll run a baseline unquantized pass, then q8 and q4 to measure latency and quality delta. often kv/prefix cache reduces end-user latency more than quantization because it avoids recomputing past tokens.

[08:20] Alex Chen: A typical pattern: warm KV cache + small batching (to keep p99 low) yields best practical latency. For throughput tests we bump batch sizes. We'll demonstrate both in the pilot.

[09:05] Priya Kapoor: On KV cache behavior - our runtime keeps a per-session KV cache and we support shared prefix caches for common prompts. warm cache cases can drop token time by 20-45% depending on sequence reuse. cold-starts still pay attention compute. We'll show cache hit metrics in the console and provide hooks to pre-warm prefixes during maintenance windows.

[10:00] Leah Wong: What's the easiest way to emulate production traffic for the pilot? we have a constrained lab with a few GPU nodes.

[10:15] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide a benchmark harness (JAR + scripts) you can run in-lab. It supports replaying logged traffic and synthetic loads. We'll run two passes: 1) interactive latency-focused (small batches, warm cache) and 2) throughput-focused (larger batches, cold start). We'll instrument token latency, tail latency, GPU utilization and memory.

[11:05] Mark Davis: Any gotchas with batching and memory? our nodes are 80GB A100s with 512GB host RAM.

[11:20] Priya Kapoor: With A100 80GB you're in a good spot. Larger batches increase throughput but also memory use - KV cache + large batch can push memory. Our autoscaling and batching autotuner recommends per-model batch caps. For variable seq lengths, dynamic batching helps but you need to cap batch wait to keep p95/p99 low. We'll include recommended config for your node size.

[12:00] Ravi Menon: For security, we'll need the checksum, sig verification steps, and the ability to validate the license blob without sending telemetry. confirm that's all supported?

[12:15] Alex Chen: Yes - tool in the bundle will verify signatures locally; no telemetry required. We'll supply SHA256 checksums and an RSA/ECDSA detached signature. For the license blob, we can support customer-wrapped keys (you provide public key) so only your HSM can unwrap. We'll document the exact CLI steps.

[13:00] Priya Kapoor: Also note driver licensing - some GPU vendors have driver redistributions restrictions. we provide pointers and, where necessary, an offline license for driver redistributions; we'll coordinate with your procurement and legal.

[13:30] Mark Davis: Sounds good. for the pilot success criteria: establish baseline latency under 200ms median for typical prompt, 95th under 350ms, and stable throughput X tokens/sec. We'll define exact numbers in the pilot doc.

[14:00] Alex Chen: Perfect. summary of next steps: we'll email the artifact checklist + signed sample, driver matrix, and pilot scope. schedule a pilot run and follow up next week to lock dates.

[14:20] Mark Davis: thanks everyone, that was very practical. Ravi and Leah will review the checklist and get back.

[14:35] Priya Kapoor: I'll drop the driver matrix and runbook after the call. Alex will follow up on pricing and license terms.

[14:50] Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll send the items by Friday.

End of meeting.
